disease.name: Stem Rot
disease.severity_index: Can cause up to 50–70% yield loss if untreated

environmental_factors.temperature_humidity: Prefers warm, humid conditions with poor drainage
environmental_factors.soil_conditions: More severe in sandy loam soils with high organic matter

region_specific_information.Andhra Pradesh: High prevalence in low-lying fields with water stagnation
region_specific_information.Telangana: More severe in rainfed areas with continuous groundnut cultivation

early_stage: Brown, water-soaked lesions at the base of stems
Wilting of lower leaves, progressing upwards
mid_stage: Formation of white fungal mycelium around the stem base
Rotted roots and weak plant anchorage
advanced_stage: Complete plant collapse due to root and stem decay
Formation of mustard seed-like sclerotia in soil
Poor pod development and shriveled seeds

crop_rotation: Deep plowing after harvest to expose fungal structures
soil_seed_treatment: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg seed
Basal application of Neem Cake @ 100 kg/acre

cultural_practices: Improve field drainage to reduce excess moisture
Solarization of soil using polythene sheets before sowing
Uprooting infected plants to prevent disease spread
biological_control: Trichoderma viride @ 2.5 kg/acre in FYM as soil application
Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed for early protection
